approach.method_basis: The Parent maintains two local molecular search regions. Each region fits a Gaussian process to its own episode's accepted scores, generates bounded graph paths from its scored center, and competes for evaluations using posterior samples in raw score units. Purchased progress expands or contracts the region; a failed minimum-size region restarts from one already scored molecule. Each regional model currently estimates its own response scale, so a one-label restart has almost no sampled variation and can receive no further feedback.
approach.novelty: Share one response amplitude estimated from all scores already accepted in the current session while retaining both local fits and their means. This makes uncertainty amplitude available to a new region before it has accumulated its own score variation, which may let ordinary sample competition purchase its candidates and restart learning. There are no completed same-Parent siblings. Historical global residual calibration changed one full-archive model's multiplier; this intervention changes the information used to set amplitude across two separately conditioned models and can widen one while shrinking the other.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-bc1f80092068 exhibits sparse regional feedback despite successful execution: 870 successful local fits, 406/435 auctions buying from only one region, 55 singleton fits, and 145 fits at response-scale floor 0.001. Two median_2 reset episodes receive no purchases during 19 and 23 subsequent fields, leaving their singleton labels unchanged. The complete Parent mean is 0.5713837397864017 (population SD 0.0299801885535169), versus n-cf8d309c06de mean 0.607030316211131; paired mean loss 0.03564657642472935. Parent global increment mass is 5.443374431161386 over 4350 optimizer evaluations, 0.0012513504439451463 per evaluation. Its local/control mechanism ran; useful conversion was refuted, not technically blocked. Sources: nodes/n-bc1f80092068/analysis.json and policy/scratch/search_policy-e8ac42d0df8b/scale-replay-summary.json. The latter indexes all fifteen historical audit-seed-N-task.json files and their exact trajectory/log inputs. This plan's read-only policy/scratch/r0051-00-improve-L01/evidence-verification.json and per-cell audits preserve and verify those historical source hashes, recount the fit/allocation statistics, and check each shared scale from its accepted prefix. The frozen replay reconstructs all 4350 original choices; sharing amplitude changes 213/435 purchase sets and introduces 573 identities, with mixed-region batches 29 to 129 and replay purchases in the two starved resets in 41/42 later batches. These are same-state decisions, not assigned scores or an adaptive performance forecast. n-707027cd2146 is a direct caution: global predictive-residual calibration activated but its complete paired score fell by 0.03515292976411536.

method_change.previous_method: Two episode-owned local count-GPs independently set raw response amplitude from each regional cohort's empirical population SD.
method_change.proposed_method: Both local conditional models use one raw response amplitude from the unique current-session accepted archive, preserving each conditional mean and normalized covariance.
method_change.rationale: Actual code Parent n-bc1f80092068 has measured singleton reset starvation and scale-floor exposure. Shared amplitude changes the source of cross-region uncertainty magnitude while leaving conditioning and controllers intact. Frozen same-state replay supports a specific exposure test; the historical global-scale loss requires a separate useful-conversion falsifier.

hypothesis: Replace episode-owned raw response amplitude by a shared current-session accepted-label amplitude. At every announcement, let A_b contain exactly the finite records already accepted into this Objective Session's unique global archive before the batch, including initial records and retired-episode records once per accepted identity/receipt. Set s_shared=max(sqrt(mean_{i in A_b}((y_i-mean(A_b))^2)),0.001), with population rather than sample variance. Keep local fitting and raw conditional mean mu_r intact, as well as normalized covariance C_r, its existing jittered Cholesky factor L_r, and original normal block Z_r. Replace s_region by s_shared only in sample_r=mu_r+s_shared*(Z_r@L_r.T), and report active predictive SD s_shared*sqrt(clamp(diag(C_r),0)). This pools amplitude evidence without pooling conditional labels or means. It changes raw observation-noise amplitude as well as raw predictive residual amplitude; standardized kernel/noise/jitter remain fixed. The hypothesized path is removal of singleton amplitude collapse, changed non-quota competition, real additional small-cohort feedback, then improved complete-panel useful gain per evaluation. No calibrated-posterior or latent-only-variance claim is made.

finding_summary.headline: Shared amplitude restores singleton feedback and improves Parent mean, while the Anchor target remains unmet.
finding_summary.insights: The experiment establishes that a singleton local model need not stay starved when amplitude information is shared: on three real restart states, 26 accepted labels came from regions that would have received zero purchases under the local-amplitude rule. Both literature-derived separations—shared amplitude from local conditioning, and amplitude aggregation from conditional solves—operated; the particular archive-moment estimator is not the sources’ estimator and these results do not establish calibrated uncertainty. The complete-panel benefit does not prove that rescued restarts caused the score gain. Across all restarted episodes, improvement per evaluation fell from 0.00017542 to 0.00012306; active-only purchases produced just 10 global improvements totaling 0.02410, while most improvement came from purchases the two rules agreed on. Late-half improvement also fell, from 1.15447 to 0.83221. Thus amplitude sharing removes a demonstrated feedback obstacle without establishing efficient later exploration. The molecular evidence supports that limitation: evaluated batches remain highly local (mean within-batch count-Tanimoto 0.7315 versus 0.4945 in generated fields), and median_2 gains more typed and generic scaffolds yet loses all three paired endpoints. Frequent unusual N-halogen chemistry and unresolved stereochemistry further separate scalar score from practical molecule quality; their contribution to score is not isolated here. A proposal or search scheme that reaches alternative coherent frameworks while preserving useful functional arrangements is the kind of method change that could address the remaining conversion limitation. This panel does not establish which such method would work, durable expected benefit, or that this approach should end.
finding_summary.results: The shared amplitude ran faithfully in all 435 batches, with both local conditional models preserved. On the same actual search states it changed 168 purchase sets, added 305 evaluated identities, and increased mixed-region batches from 55 to 88. Singleton-region purchases increased from 156 under the local-amplitude replay to 186 actual accepted labels. All 19 real restarted regions received feedback immediately; the Parent had two restarted regions that received none over 19 and 23 subsequent batches. The whole-panel global improvement per evaluation rose from 0.00125135 to 0.00129697, so the registered exposure and useful-conversion predictions are supported. Mean endpoint score rose from 0.571384 to 0.584614, a paired gain of 0.013230 across three seeds, although one seed lost. The formal Anchor mean is 0.607030: the Child remains 0.022417 below it and fails the separate +0.002 performance target. Task-safety margins were not supplied, so no new task-safety classification is made.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic analogues retain N-halogen liabilities, extreme size tails and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment describes actual evaluated molecules, not algorithm activation. The frozen digest and all fifteen Child Search trajectories and fifteen published code-Parent trajectories were read. Each node contributes 4,350 optimizer proposals, with 870 per task; the initial records were read separately and excluded from descriptor counts. context.comparison reports both child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 against n-bc1f80092068; no requested trajectory is missing. No unpurchased candidate fields, replay-only alternatives, heldout results or Confirmation evidence were inspected. Thus these counts characterize evaluated optimizer output only and cannot describe all generated fields or assign responsibility to a component. No separate Anchor molecular comparison was performed. All audited optimizer SMILES parse with RDKit, but parseability is not evidence of isolation, stability, synthetic accessibility or pharmacology. The Child contains rings in 4,197 proposals and aromatic atoms in 4,151. The digest's per-task ring-closure and aromatic-text rates agree with a ring-rich population, rather than missing ring chemistry. The repertoire includes indoles and other fused heteroaromatics, carbonyl/nitrile substituents, amine-bearing saturated rings, linked polyheteroaromatics, imide-like dicarbonyl cores and unusual larger or small fused rings. Many local series retain a recognizable inherited core, despite substantial typed and generic scaffold variation; scaffold counts do not establish useful diversity. The Child has 134 proposals below six heavy atoms and 245 above fifty, versus 133 and 284 for the Parent. It contains 1,017 proposals with N-halogen adjacency and 104 with O-halogen adjacency, versus 1,228 and 336 in the Parent; the reduction is not uniform across tasks. All Child proposals have net formal charge zero. RDKit identifies potential tetrahedral centers in 2,113 proposals, but none has an assigned tetrahedral center, consistent with the digest's zero stereocentre-text rate. Neutral SMILES do not prove lack of ionizable amines, and absent stereo specification does not establish that these scores would reward stereoisomer selection. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable overall: familiar medicinal fragments coexist with N-F/N-Cl/N-Br, O-halogen, strained-looking ring junctions and unusually large recombinations. The chemistry judgments and transferable gaps below originate in n-7d1e6230ecce under this frozen Search panel, with n-bc1f80092068 used only as a paired descriptive baseline. No score-dependent claim here establishes a molecular mechanism, prospective performance or component attribution. Request and digest source: policy/requests/r0051-00-improve-L01-molecular-assess-202a0f7ed01409d5.json. The task citations identify every audit and underlying input. Each audit records its task, frozen Search seed, request SHA256, original staging path/SHA256, byte-exact in-run copy and published Parent path/SHA256. Child evidence remains a provenance-preserving scratch snapshot because no finalized Child archive exists.

per_task.generated_character: The evaluated population has median 25 heavy atoms and spans 2 to 56. It is dominated by aromatic/fused heteroaromatic carbonyl compounds: methoxy/methyl/nitrile indole-like cores, pyridyl ketone substituents, aryl amides and later unusual ring-expanded or small-annulated analogues. The best observed molecule, COc1c(C)ccc(C(=O)Cc2cnc3cc2C3)[nH]ccc1C#N, has 24 heavy atoms and a nonstandard larger aza-aromatic ring plus a small annulation, so its graph should not be presented as an ordinary indole. The more familiar nitrile/methoxy indole ketone COc1c(C#N)cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Cc3ccc(C)nc3)cc2c1C is also among the high scores. Seed 2 instead retains an N-brominated aryl amide series. Across all seeds, 414 of 870 proposals have N-halogen bonds, versus 188 in the Parent; the median heavy-atom count is unchanged at 25. Typed/generic nonempty scaffold counts are 298/161 versus the Parent's 258/106, but many differences retain these aromatic carbonyl families. Search sources (derived audit followed by its byte-exact Child trajectory and published Parent trajectory): policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/inputs/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-bc1f80092068/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/inputs/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-bc1f80092068/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/inputs/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-bc1f80092068/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl.
liabilities: N-halogen substitution is common and increased relative to the Parent; N-brominated amides and O-halogen fragments raise stability and handling questions that the scores do not resolve.

The highest-scoring graph's larger unsaturated ring/small annulation has uncertain synthetic accessibility; oversized repeat-like aromatic products and sub-six-heavy-atom fragments consume evaluated output without demonstrating a coherent usable molecule.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently preserve a complete medium-sized aromatic carbonyl framework: tiny fragments and oversized duplications coexist with the best series. The observed scores support that distinction, not a new target-specific motif.

A uniformly conventional, synthetically credible ring-and-linker series is absent from the upper-score sample: the leading structure has unusual ring topology, and another seed favors an N-bromo amide. No unobserved alternative can be declared score-improving from these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The expanded/annulated nitrile ketone scores 0.5423261445466404 and the conventional indole ketone 0.5188745216627708, above the shared initial aromatic amide's 0.3051048083696145. These observations associate the upper scores with a retained medium-sized aromatic carbonyl/nitrile framework, not with indiscriminate growth: the highly recombined N-fluoro structure cited below scores 1.508112452773851e-35, while OF and ClCl both score zero. The seed-2 N-bromo amide reaches 0.4478476056206344, showing that a concerning N-halogen group is tolerated in this series rather than automatically penalized. Child endpoint changes relative to the Parent are negative in seeds 0 and 2 and tied in seed 1; the tied best score occurs for different structures. These are associations within sampled families; neither the nitrile nor the unusual ring system is independently established as causal.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most elaborated output family: median 37 heavy atoms, range 1 to 108, and 203 of 870 evaluated proposals above fifty heavy atoms. High scores occur in N-linked polyheteroaromatics, including a 32-heavy-atom fluorinated/brominated structure with two annulated aza-aromatic blocks linked by NH and a 40-heavy-atom pair of carbonyl-containing heterocycles carrying ketone, imine and haloalkyl appendages. The latter series gives equal scores for several substantial substituent changes. The Parent was larger overall, with median 44 heavy atoms and 242 proposals above fifty; Child versus Parent N-halogen occurrence falls from 287 to 23 and O-halogen occurrence from 214 to 25. The Child's 450 typed and 347 generic nonempty scaffolds versus 418/342 in the Parent show ample graph variation, not absence of rings, but do not show that all structures are makeable. Search sources (derived audit followed by its byte-exact Child trajectory and published Parent trajectory): policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/audit-seed-0-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/inputs/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-bc1f80092068/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/audit-seed-1-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/inputs/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-bc1f80092068/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/audit-seed-2-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/inputs/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-bc1f80092068/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl.
liabilities: Extensive aromatic fusion, multiple halo substituents and large linked blocks make some structures synthetically demanding; large repeated heterocyclic products remain frequent.

The carbonyl-rich branch contains imines, alkyl halides and several carbonyl-bearing appendages whose stability and selectivity are untested. Better graph validity or a higher scalar score does not resolve these liabilities.
missing_features: There is no deficit of aromatic rings or heteroatoms. What is not consistently retained is a compact, chemically manageable decorated framework: the large tail reaches 108 heavy atoms despite the strongest cited examples being much smaller.

A broadly explored set of equally connected but simpler stable linker/decorator alternatives is not demonstrated by the leading, locally related polyheteroaromatic series. The narrow score spread and equal-score substitutions do not identify a unique missing substituent.

The shared initial imide-containing aromatic molecule scores 0.548381482770623, while F, C and ClCl score 0.5. Thus an organized, substituted heteroaromatic framework is associated with the improvement above the observed fragment floor. The seed-2 terminal N-methylated bridge analogue scores 0.6209299209433203 and the reduced imine analogue 0.61634565330557; retaining the NH link and unsaturated side chain is associated with higher scores in these examples, but many other coupled changes preclude a general rule. All three paired Child endpoints exceed their Parent endpoints. That accompanies changed chemical families and fewer N/O-halogen bonds, and does not attribute the score change to removing those bonds.

per_task.generated_character: These molecules provide the clearest amine-bearing saturated-ring chemistry. The evaluated median is 29 heavy atoms, with a 1-to-108 range; seed-level medians are 28, 31 and 23, compared with the Parent's 35, 32.5 and 33. The highest seed-2 family combines N-propylpyrrolidine, a benzylic halogenated link, an indane-like aromatic/saturated ring system, phenol and sometimes an aniline or additional linker NH. The best molecule has 21 heavy atoms. Seed 1 instead produces a larger N-methyl ring with sulfoxide or ketone, two phenolic aromatic regions and an aminomethyl group. The broad structural types are medicinally recognizable and less exotic than several other tasks' top products, although the exact halo-substituted stereochemical structures are not validated compounds. There are 835 proposals with potential tetrahedral centers and none with assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry. Typed/generic scaffold coverage is 355/234 versus 352/234 for the Parent. Search sources (derived audit followed by its byte-exact Child trajectory and published Parent trajectory): policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/audit-seed-0-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/inputs/seed-0/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-bc1f80092068/seed-0/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/audit-seed-1-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/inputs/seed-1/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-bc1f80092068/seed-1/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/audit-seed-2-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0051-00-molecular/inputs/seed-2/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-bc1f80092068/seed-2/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl.
liabilities: Benzylic or alpha-amino halogenated links and multiply substituted ring junctions pose chemical stability and synthetic selectivity questions; no assay or synthesis evidence establishes them as practical compounds.
Unassigned stereochemistry is pervasive in this highly three-dimensional family. Neutral encodings also leave ionization states unspecified rather than proving these tertiary amines stay neutral.
missing_features: Basic amine centers and mixed aromatic/saturated ring systems are present in the strongest observed molecules. The missing representational capability is explicit stereoisomer identity in their substituted rings and benzylic linkers; this audit cannot show that stereo resolution would improve the recorded objective.
The lower-scoring fragments fail to retain the combined amine-plus-aromatic architecture. No additional unseen receptor-specific pharmacophore can be inferred from these molecules and scores alone.

There is no evidence of an absent ring, nitrogen or carbonyl capability. A particular unsampled scaffold cannot be prescribed from this shallow observed gradient, and a synthetically conventional alternative with equal scoring features has not been demonstrated.

The best seed-0 family has a fused dicarbonyl N-heteroaromatic core, an unsaturated N-containing five-membered ring bearing aminomethyl and fluorine, and a substituted cyclopentadiene-like ring. The 29-heavy-atom best graph contains three N-F bonds, not simply ordinary C-F substituents. liabilities: Repeated N-F bonds on carbonyl-adjacent and amine-like nitrogen centers are a major synthetic/stability concern in the highest-score family; carbon-bound fluorine and N-bound fluorine should not be conflated.

Unsaturated small-ring substituents, strained-looking annulations and unspecified stereochemistry limit confidence in practical medicinal chemistry. Tiny fragments and large recombinations occupy the opposite low-score tails.
missing_features: The generator does not demonstrate consistent access to equally competitive, stable fluorinated frameworks that avoid unusual N-halogen and small-ring connectivity. This is a chemistry-quality gap, not evidence that eliminating N-F would raise this objective.

Explicit stereochemistry is absent despite substituted partially saturated rings in the strongest seed-0 products. No stereochemical scoring benefit or missing target-specific motif is established by these trajectories.

Its corresponding terminal ring thiol analogue scores 0.7098514946189204, while the analogue lacking that terminal F/S substituent scores 0.6981586060468723. These high scores coexist with repeated N-F bonds; this score is not a demonstrated synthetic-plausibility screen. The best seed-1 molecule without direct N-F bonds scores 0.6174769250330556, so direct N-halogen bonding is not universally necessary for a substantial score. The shared initial imide-containing aromatic molecule is only 0.0020944534688323298. The large recombination cited below scores 2.3956869936426998e-105, and the late small fluoroalkene C=C(C)CCF is 2.7106822186457567e-17. The observed gradient thus associates a particular medium-sized fluorinated heterocyclic organization with improvement, rather than fluorine count or molecular growth alone. Paired endpoints rise in seeds 0 and 2 and fall in seed 1; the highest gain is accompanied by unusual N-fluorinated chemistry, not established practical molecular quality.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-7d1e6230ecce, frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, evaluated optimizer population only: 1,017 of 4,350 proposals contain N-halogen bonds and 104 contain O-halogen bonds. One strongest-scoring cited structure contains three N-F bonds; another high-scoring series contains N-brominated amides. The paired n-bc1f80092068 baseline contains 1,228 and 336 such proposals, so the liability persists despite a panel-wide reduction and varies by series. The per-task audits and underlying trajectories cited above establish the counts; these associations do not identify the responsible component.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve chemically conventional bond types when elaborating otherwise recognizable aromatic and carbonyl frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A future task-agnostic chemistry capability would need to offer conventional alternatives that preserve an observed scaffold's size, heteroatom arrangement and attachment geometry without routinely creating N-X or O-X bonds. Any benefit would have to be measured using accepted feedback; the current high scores do not justify treating these liabilities as automatically score-decreasing or silently adding a chemistry reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-7d1e6230ecce under the same frozen Search/evaluated-output conditions: 134 proposals have fewer than six heavy atoms and 245 exceed fifty, versus 133 and 284 in n-bc1f80092068. The cited examples include tiny molecules at zero or the observed score floor, and very large repeated heterocyclic structures with extremely low scores, alongside substantially higher-scoring medium-sized structures. Large molecules are not uniformly bad: one output family retains many large proposals. Counts and counterexamples come from the per-task audits, not an inferred universal size optimum.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot yet reliably vary a scaffold while preserving a complete, bounded-size molecular architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need structurally meaningful scaffold and substituent changes that can retain connected functional architecture while exploring size in both directions. Use the current session's measured returns to determine where that matters; these observations do not justify a universal size cutoff, additional oracle calls or a fixed target-specific template.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-7d1e6230ecce, evaluated optimizer molecules in the frozen Search panel: RDKit identifies potential tetrahedral centers in 2,113 of 4,350 proposals but no assigned tetrahedral centers. The digest independently reports zero stereocentre-text rate for every task, and the paired Parent also lacks assignments. Highly scored amine-bearing saturated rings and substituted partially saturated heterocycles exemplify this absence; neither descriptor establishes that an objective rewards stereo resolution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits stereochemically unresolved structures even when its evaluated output creates potential tetrahedral centers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator intended to supply concrete chemical candidates would need a consistent way to represent and retain stereochemical identity through graph changes. Whether searching those identities improves a score is an unresolved empirical question, and any later investigation must stay task-agnostic and preserve its own authorized evaluation conditions.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-7d1e6230ecce and paired n-bc1f80092068 under the same frozen Search conditions: one family increases typed/generic nonempty scaffold coverage from 513/316 to 607/434 while every paired endpoint decreases. Other strong examples remain unusual fused dicarbonyl, N-fluorinated or larger-ring analogues of recurring cores. The full trajectories also contain conventional amines, aromatic rings and carbonyls, so this is not an absence of those building blocks and cannot establish a globally inaccessible scaffold.
transferable_gaps.gap: Rich ring variation is present, but reliable access to chemically interpretable alternative frameworks beyond recurring local families is not demonstrated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A future task-agnostic capability would need to preserve useful functional arrangements while reaching alternative complete frameworks, with structural interpretability assessed separately from graph novelty. Measure useful diversity through real feedback; more unique Murcko scaffolds, heteroatoms or ring sizes alone cannot serve as evidence of a better generator or attribution to one component.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
